annotations.text:
Four directions for the Translator screen — same content and the same layout skeleton, four different visual languages. The text ⇄ Morse toggle works in all four: tap it to see the reverse direction.

Pick one and I'll build the full screen set in it — Translator, Speech, Tap decode, Settings, Learn, Tips, permission gates, phone and tablet.

The app name is still open: "MORSE" is a placeholder wordmark, not a proposal.

A · TELEGRAPH DESK

Why: leans on the history — paper, brass, inked marks, a tape strip. The Learn and Tips pages feel native here rather than bolted on.

Trade-off: a light paper ground is wrong for night use, and the warmth can read as decorative rather than precise.

B · SIGNAL LAMP

Why: reads as an instrument. The dark ground makes torch flash and tap timing feel native, and the amber pulse IS the signal.

Trade-off: the safest of the four — dark utility apps all look roughly like this. Least memorable in a store listing.

C · DOT & DASH

Why: the code itself is the design — oversized marks, heavy type, one hot colour. The most distinctive and the most screenshot-friendly.

Trade-off: costs the most to keep responsive phone → tablet, and the dense screens (Settings, Learn) will fight the expressive layout.

D · PRACTICE DECK

Why: leans on the learning angle FOUNDATION.md calls out — cards, soft ground, visible progress. Pairs naturally with tap-practice and Tips.

Trade-off: the least distinctive; risks looking like every other learning app.
